item.title: Microsoft Announces Voluntary Exit Offer for Up to 60,000 Employees, Including AI Teams
item.description:
Microsoft Announces Voluntary Exit Offer for Up to 60,000 Employees, Including AI Teams

Microsoft is extending a voluntary buyout program to as many as 60,000 staff members across the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and India. The offer reaches a broader slice of the company’s roughly 223,000 employees and includes many teams that work on artificial‑intelligence products.

🔍 Overview

  • Voluntary exit offers are being made to up to 60,000 employees.
  • The program is intended to allow staff to leave with “financial support and career planning resources” while the company trims headcount without another round of layoffs.
  • The offer is described as “new for us” by Microsoft chief people officer Amy Coleman.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Eligibility covers a wide range of groups, including:
    • AI experiences, Copilot, CoreAI, Windows + Devices, Xbox, finance, and human‑resources teams.
    • Cloud + AI, MicrosoftAI, and corporate, external, and legal‑affairs teams (partial participation).
  • Teams not participating:
    • Marketing, commercial business, discovery and quantum, and security teams.
  • The offer is not based on age, length of service, or performance, according to an internal HR note.
  • It differs from an earlier voluntary‑retirement program that was limited to about 9,000 U.S. employees meeting a combined age‑and‑service threshold of 70.
Team Group Participation Status
AI experiences, Copilot, CoreAI, Windows + Devices, Xbox, finance, HR Eligible (full)
Cloud + AI, MicrosoftAI, corporate, external, legal affairs Eligible (partial)
Marketing, commercial business, discovery & quantum, security Not eligible

💡 Why It Matters

  • The voluntary exit offer follows a layoff of 4,800 employees earlier in the year, primarily affecting Xbox and commercial‑sales staff.
  • Microsoft’s leadership frames the program as a way to “help people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft.”
  • The company states it may consider future voluntary exit offers “where there is a business and workforce need.”

📢 Official Statements

  • Amy Coleman wrote, “The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us. We’ll learn from it. At the same time, we’ll keep helping people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft.”
  • An internal HR note confirms the offer “isn’t based on age, length of service, or performance.”

📅 Recent Context

  • The voluntary exit program arrives months after the 4,800‑person layoff.
  • Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is reported to be planning new rounds of layoffs.
  • The new offer does not target Microsoft’s commercial‑sales teams, distinguishing it from the earlier retirement program.

#Microsoft #Workforce #AI

Source: Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 employees

item.title: SpaceX and Tesla Explore AI Merger and Joint Superintelligence Projects
item.description:
SpaceX and Tesla Explore AI Merger and Joint Superintelligence Projects

SpaceX and Tesla have officially created special committees to explore a merger while simultaneously collaborating on superintelligence software development. The move comes as SpaceX’s AI‑related revenue surged in the latest quarter.

🔍 Overview

  • SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss a merger!
  • Elon Musk said on the recent SpaceX earnings call that “there’s a lot of merit to combining” SpaceX and Tesla.
  • A quoted statement notes, “There’s a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software.”

📊 Financial Snapshot

  • In its Q3 earnings on Tuesday, SpaceX reported $7.56 billion in revenue from the artificial intelligence — sorry, super intelligence — division.
  • The subcategory “SI solutions & infrastructure revenues” (which includes Grok, Cursor, and the neocloud business) jumped to $7 billion, more than three times the previous quarter.
  • $608 million of that increase came from Cursor being “stapled on.”
  • Analyst Gil Luria (DA Davidson) said most of the remaining $7 billion is likely from renting compute to Anthropic and Google, with Grok contributing less.
  • For comparison, Anthropic’s leaked S‑1 shows $16.3 billion in revenue in the first half of the year from its frontier models.
  • Tesla’s Q3 results were weak, described as “earnings sucked — a second consecutive quarter of declining profits.”

🤝 Joint AI Initiatives

Project Description Current Status (per filings)
Terafab Chip‑making venture in Texas intended to supply Musk’s companies with chips; Intel is a partner. “In the very early stages… we and Tesla have not finalized a variety of details…including financial terms, intellectual property rights, and the ultimate term of our collaboration.”
Macrohard AI project that lets people simulate software already made by Microsoft. Not mentioned in the last 10‑Q; details remain undeclared.
  • SpaceX’s S‑1 from May notes both Terafab and Macrohard are early‑stage collaborations with no finalized terms.
  • Intel’s CEO reiterated commitment to the partnership but clarified Intel is not obligated to remain part of Terafab, and the S‑1 warns a definitive agreement may never be reached.
  • Intel’s Thomas Hannaford did not respond to inquiries about any interim signing.
  • On a recent SpaceX investor call, Musk claimed Terafab will reach volume production in the second half of 2028 and will have its first test chip in May or June 2027.
  • When asked whether orders for cutting‑edge equipment had been placed, Musk did not answer.

🏭 Existing Business Ties

  • SpaceX bought $131 million of low‑selling Cybertrucks from Tesla.
  • SpaceX has previously held Tesla bonds.

📈 Why It Matters

  • The revenue surge indicates SpaceX’s AI division is scaling quickly, positioning the company as a significant player alongside established AI firms.
  • Formal merger discussions could align the two companies’ massive capital resources, potentially accelerating joint AI hardware and software development.
  • Early‑stage projects like Terafab and Macrohard show a strategic intent to control both the compute stack (chips) and application layer (software simulation), though concrete agreements remain unsettled.

All statements are drawn directly from publicly disclosed earnings calls, filings, and analyst commentary.

#SpaceX #Tesla #AI #Superintelligence #Merger

Source: Sure, let’s smoosh SpaceX and Tesla together, who cares

item.title: Silicon Valley Leaders Adopt Trump's 'Super Intelligence' Rebrand
item.description:
Silicon Valley Leaders Adopt Trump’s “Super Intelligence” Rebrand

President Donald Trump announced his plans to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” prompting a swift response from several tech executives.

🔍 Overview

  • Trump declared that the White House considers anyone using the term “Artificial Intelligence” instead of the new term “Super Intelligence” THE ENEMY.
  • The broader population is still using AI, but a number of Silicon Valley’s most powerful figures are falling in line with Trump’s rebrand.

🤝 Silicon Valley Alignment

  • Musk, Benioff, Huang, and now Nadella have all capitulated to Trump’s ‘super intelligence’ rebrand.
  • During Trump’s second term, Silicon Valley has repeatedly tried to ingratiate itself with the administration, after having a much more contentious relationship during his first term.

🏢 Corporate Renames & Commitments

Leader Company Action
Elon Musk SpaceX Promised to rename SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI
Marc Benioff Salesforce Announced rename of AIForce to SIForce
Jensen Huang Nvidia Attended summit where executive order was announced; committed $1 billion to scientific advancement that includes “super intelligence research”
Satya Nadella Microsoft Attended same AI summit as Huang; in a post calling for an “emergency brake” for AI, repeatedly referred to the technology as “super intelligence”

📜 Executive Order & Government Directive

  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang attended the summit where the executive order requiring government agencies to use the term “super intelligence” was announced.
  • Huang also stated he believes the danger posed by AI is overblown.

💭 Why It Matters

  • The coordinated rename effort shows a notable shift toward aligning corporate language with the administration’s terminology.
  • Large financial commitments (e.g., Nvidia’s $1 billion) are being framed as support for “super intelligence research.”
  • High‑profile leaders publicly endorsing the term may influence public and governmental perception of AI.

#Trump #SuperIntelligence #AIRebrand #TechLeadership

Source: Silicon Valley is falling in line with Trump’s attempt to rename AI
